repo_model.summary: This repository is a RelBench generic-search starter workspace: main.py emits baseline validation and test predictions for each task family, while kapso_datasets documents and supports the prediction contract and kapso_evaluation runs isolated official scoring.

entrypoints.how_to_run: python main.py --debug for the fast/debug build, or python main.py for the full run.

where_to_edit.role: Primary candidate implementation and prediction-generation logic; the seeded baseline is intended to be replaced.
Reusable task-loading, prediction-saving, temporal-safety, and MAP@K helpers.
Reference for required prediction files, shapes, data access, and validation behavior.
Provided scoring pipeline; do not modify evaluation-suite code.

claims.statement: main.py obtains the dataset and task from environment variables using RelBench with download=False, sizes outputs from the validation and test tables, and detects rolling evaluation when the cached validation table is empty or absent.

evidence.description: Reads the RelBench dataset name from the environment.
Loads the task without downloading.
Builds the cached validation parquet path.
Sets the validation row count and rolling flag.
Reads the test row count.

claims.statement: The seeded candidate branches by task family: recommendations receive tiled integer rankings, binary classification receives 0.5 probabilities, multiclass classification receives uniform class scores, and other tasks receive the training-target median.

evidence.description: Starts the recommendation-task branch.
Creates constant binary-classification probabilities.
Starts the multiclass branch.
Creates uniform multiclass scores.
Uses the fallback branch for other task types.
Computes the training-target median for the fallback.

claims.statement: kapso_datasets.common.load_task constructs a TaskContext containing the dataset, task, database, and train/validation/test RelBench tables; train and validation include labels while test contains only seed inputs and timestamps.

evidence.description: Defines the TaskContext container.
Documents that training rows include labels.
Documents that test rows contain seed ids and timestamps only.
Defines the task-loading helper.
Loads the dataset from the sanitized cache without downloading.
Loads the train table.
Loads the test table.

claims.statement: The provided grader runs main.py as an isolated child process, loads the resulting prediction files, validates them against the official validation table, computes RelBench metrics, and emits a machine-readable score manifest.

evidence.description: States that the candidate runs in an isolated child subprocess.
Builds the candidate command for debug or full fidelity.
Starts the isolated candidate subprocess.
Locates the validation and test prediction artifacts.
Computes official validation metrics.
Prints the machine-readable evaluation manifest.

claims.statement: In rolling evaluation, the grader invokes the candidate once per snapshot, reads each tick's test predictions and row indices, then assembles them into the official row-order prediction vector.

evidence.description: Defines the rolling-harness execution path.
Creates an isolated stage for each snapshot.
Runs the candidate for each rolling tick.
Loads the snapshot row indices.
Collects per-tick predictions and indices.
Writes the assembled prediction vector.

claims.statement: Every run must write both val_predictions.npy and test_predictions.npy with rows positionally aligned to the corresponding RelBench tables; validation predictions must be out-of-sample and must not use validation labels for training.

evidence.description: Requires both prediction files after every run with positional row alignment.
Requires validation predictions to be out-of-sample.
Restricts train-plus-validation usage to the test-producing model.

claims.statement: Prediction formats are task-specific: binary and regression use float vectors, multiclass uses an (N, C) float matrix, and recommendation uses an (N, K) integer matrix of distinct destination ids in range.

evidence.description: Defines binary, regression, and multiclass prediction formats.
Defines recommendation integer ranking requirements.

claims.statement: Data access must use the sanitized read-only cache with download=False; test labels are physically absent and must not be probed.

evidence.description: Requires RelBench API access with download=False and describes the sanitized cache.
States that test labels are physically absent.
Documents loading from the sanitized cache without downloads.
Calls get_dataset with download=False.
Calls get_task with download=False.

claims.statement: The search score is the official validation primary metric; test metrics are private and are not available during the search loop.

evidence.description: Defines the official validation primary metric as the search score.
States that test metrics are computed privately.
Places the selected validation metric in the manifest score.

claims.statement: The harness runs python main.py --debug as a fast end-to-end pipeline check and python main.py for the full training run; both modes must produce the required prediction artifacts.

evidence.description: States that the harness runs the program twice per experiment.
Defines the debug command.
Defines the full command.
States that outputs are loaded, validated, and scored after each run.
Requires both files after every run, including debug.

claims.statement: After writing predictions, kapso_datasets/check_predictions.py can validate file existence, shapes, dtypes, finiteness, and binary ranges; successful validation prints an all-checks-passed message.

evidence.description: Defines the checker entrypoint.
Checks both validation and test splits.
Checks recommendation shape and integer dtype.
Checks non-recommendation prediction shapes.
Rejects non-finite predictions.
Prints per-split success status.
Prints the final all-checks-passed status.

claims.statement: A fast official dry run is invoked with the grader's --fidelity fast mode, which runs main.py --debug while still scoring the complete validation split and reporting the official metric manifest.

evidence.description: Documents the grader CLI.
Maps fast fidelity to main.py --debug.
States that validation rows are not subsampled.
Adds --debug for fast fidelity.
Prints official validation metrics.
Prints the machine-readable manifest.

claims.statement: In the seeded baseline, --debug does not select a different modeling path; it is only reflected in the final diagnostic message, so debug and full prediction logic are otherwise identical.

evidence.description: Prediction branching begins without checking debug mode.
Output handling also does not branch on debug mode.
The debug flag is only interpolated into the status message.

claims.statement: Rolling snapshots are special: an empty validation table marks the invocation as rolling, main.py skips writing a validation file, and the grader consumes each tick's test file before assembling the final vectors.

evidence.description: Documents the empty validation table in rolling snapshots.
Marks the run as rolling when validation has zero rows.
Writes validation predictions only for non-rolling runs.
Requires the per-tick test prediction file.
Assembles the rolling prediction vector.

claims.statement: The recommendation baseline emits ids 0 through K-1 without consulting num_dst_nodes; the checker warns about out-of-range ids or duplicate rows rather than failing those conditions.

evidence.description: Creates recommendation ids as arange(k).
Tiles those ids for test predictions.
Warns when recommendation ids are outside the destination range.
Warns when rows contain duplicate ids.

claims.statement: load_task defaults to database rows up to the test timestamp; autocomplete tasks must explicitly pass upto_test_timestamp=False to use post-test-cutoff entity rows as inputs, whose targets are blanked.

evidence.description: Defaults upto_test_timestamp to True.
Documents the autocomplete exception.
States that post-test rows are inputs with blanked targets.
Passes the timestamp option into dataset database loading.

claims.statement: The evaluation suite is self-contained with the Python standard library, numpy, and relbench; the documentation says no additional setup is needed beyond those packages.

evidence.description: Lists stdlib, numpy, and relbench as grader imports.
States that configuration arrives through environment variables.
States that Python with relbench and numpy is sufficient.

claims.statement: The candidate requires handler-provided environment variables for dataset/task identity, the sanitized cache, and the per-run output directory; the grader additionally requires the primary metric, work directory, and timeout settings.

evidence.description: Requires RELBENCH_DATASET.
Requires RELBENCH_TASK.
Requires RELBENCH_CACHE_DIR.
Requires KAPSO_RUN_DATA_DIR.
Lists the primary metric and archive environment variables.
Lists full and debug timeout variables.

book.summary: This repository is a RelBench generic-search starter workspace: main.py emits baseline validation and test predictions for each task family, while kapso_datasets documents and supports the prediction contract and kapso_evaluation runs isolated official scoring.

toc.title: Architecture
toc.one_liner: A root candidate script uses RelBench task tables to produce predictions, with helper utilities and an isolated grader handling validation, scoring, and archival.

toc.title: Entrypoints
toc.one_liner: Run the candidate directly for debug/full modes or invoke the provided grader for official evaluation.

toc.title: Where to edit
toc.one_liner: Put candidate modeling and prediction changes in main.py; use the starter helpers for contract-compliant data access and output.

toc.title: Invariants
toc.one_liner: Predictions must satisfy split alignment, task-specific shape/type, leakage, and scoring contracts.

toc.title: Testing
toc.one_liner: Use the debug run, local prediction checker, and fast grader to validate changes before full evaluation.

toc.title: Gotchas
toc.one_liner: The starter baseline has intentionally trivial behavior and special rolling-cache handling that can surprise model implementers.

toc.title: Dependencies
toc.one_liner: The runtime depends on Python with relbench and numpy, plus handler-provided environment variables and a prepared sanitized cache.
